comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Easier to hit on Windows where the overlay scrollbar still reserves space in the content box.

content.text: Easier to hit on Windows where the overlay scrollbar still reserves space in the content box.
In the editor table UI, dragging the resize handle on the last column snaps that column width to 0px on mouseup if the drag ends within 4px of the table right edge. Other columns resize smoothly.

Last column should clamp to a minimum width (currently 48px for others) like every other column. The last handle max delta is computed against container width minus prior columns, but the clamp runs before subtracting scrollbar width (12-16px), so the allowed width becomes negative and snaps to zero.
Tables with a collapsed last column hide cell content and are hard to recover without undo. Applying the same min-width clamp after scrollbar compensation keeps the last column visible.
